methods.description: lifecycle

methods.name: BufferId
methods.description: Hand the engine id out -- for a graph that wants this sound as a source. An ENGINE handle, not a pointer, so it obeys the house law.

methods.name: Frames
methods.description: readers: they return DATA and keep their names

methods.name: SampleAt
methods.description: ONE sample. 1-based frame and channel, like every Haro face.

methods.name: ToList
methods.description: The samples of one channel, as a Haro list. DATA, so To... is right. Be aware this crosses the FFI once per sample -- fine for a look at a few thousand frames, wrong for a whole song.

methods.name: ResampleTo
methods.description: verbs that change the sound ---------------------------------------- Resample to a new rate. QUALITY is sinc unless you ask otherwise -- SN1 measured sinc at 97x the accuracy of linear for 26x the cost, and still 150x faster than real time, so it is the right default.

methods.name: ToWavBytes
methods.description: The symmetric half of loading from memory, and its absence was a real gap: a sound could be decoded FROM bytes but not encoded back TO them, so handing a buffer to another tier meant a temporary file. VC1 went to some trouble to keep a voice out of the filesystem; without this, VC3 would have put it straight back to feed a recogniser.

methods.name: MixIn
methods.description: 16-bit by default: it is what everything reads, and SN1 measured the round-trip error at 4.18e-5, one quantum. Ask for 32 when you are handing the file back to another stage rather than to a listener. ADD another sound into this one from pnSeconds in, scaled by pnGain -- notes laid on a timeline. Refused when the sample rates differ: a note mixed at the wrong rate would be a different pitch, silently.

methods.name: Play
methods.description: hearing it ---------------------------------------------------------- PLAY IT, and wait for it to finish. There is no sample-player in the engine -- the device sink plays a STREAM -- so the face builds the smallest graph that can carry this sound and runs it. That is what a declarative face is for: the caller says "play", not "make a graph, start a producer thread, open a device, wait, then take it all down".

methods.name: ToSpectrum
methods.description: To...() because these RETURN things. A spectrum is a stzSoundGrid: rows by columns of numbers, with x_step and y_step saying what a row and a column MEAN. Drawing one is the graphics plane's job, and keeping that boundary is what makes the analysis assertable -- "the 1 kHz sine is in the 1 kHz bin" is a claim about numbers; "the picture looks right" is a claim about nothing. The magnitude spectrum of one window. Default 4096 points: about 12 Hz resolution at 48 kHz, which resolves musical pitch without smearing time.

methods.name: ToSpectrogram
methods.description: Frequency against time: one row per window. MULTICORE by default -- every row is an independent FFT over a different slice of the same immutable buffer, which is the one analysis here that parallelises without an argument.

methods.name: DominantFrequency
methods.description: The strongest frequency present, in hertz.

methods.name: ToOnsets
methods.description: Where notes START, in seconds -- a one-row grid of times.

methods.name: Tempo
methods.description: Beats per minute, or -1 when there are too few onsets to say -- which is a better answer than a confident number derived from two events.

methods.name: Loudness
methods.description: The standard's K-weighting coefficients are specified at 48 kHz, and the engine REFUSES any other rate rather than applying them anyway. So the face resamples a COPY when it has to -- the caller's sound is not touched, and nobody gets a plausible-looking wrong number.

methods.name: MomentaryLoudness
methods.description: MomentaryLoudness is the standard's own 400 ms window, ungated, taking the LOUDEST such window rather than a mean -- averaging an earcon against the silence around it answers nothing. BS.1770 arithmetic used as specified, so it is LUFS without qualification.

methods.name: LoudnessOfSupport
methods.description: The same K-weighting and the same formula over the sound's OWN length. NOT a standard LUFS figure, and LoudnessMetric() says so -- because the alternative is answering the standard's question wrongly instead of answering a different question honestly. A 60 ms earcon at peak 0.5 reads -9.26 here against -9.27 for the same tone at 400 ms: the two agree to a hundredth of a decibel where the standard has an opinion, which is what makes this trustworthy where it does not.

methods.name: LoudnessMetric
methods.description: What the number means, so it never travels without its method.

methods.name: Vowels
methods.description: The five vowels, and the first two formants each sits on at a pitch -- what the guard holds the rendered spectrum against.

methods.name: Vowel
methods.description: One vowel at a pitch (a note name or Hz) for `pnSeconds`.

methods.name: Sing
methods.description: SINGING -- gated by the verdict. Refused, with the reason, until the author has heard the formant voice and called it singing.

methods.name: Reshape
methods.description: Start over with a different shape. Only legal before anything is added.

methods.name: OutputNode
methods.description: Which node the graph currently hands to the world, as an index. A caller rarely needs this; a TRANSPORT does, because it has to reach behind the names and put something after whatever the output turned out to be.

methods.name: AddMasterGain
methods.description: This is what a transport fades on pause. It exists as a verb here rather than in the transport because only the graph knows what its output IS -- and putting one gain at the end means a pause is one click-free ramp instead of a walk over every voice, whatever the caller built upstream.

methods.name: NameIt
methods.description: naming -------------------------------------------------------------- Label the LAST node added, so later verbs can refer to it by name.

methods.name: NodeNamed
methods.description: Resolve a name OR a raw node number to a node index. Unknown names are an error the caller hears about, never a silent 0.

methods.name: AddOscillator
methods.description: the sources --------------------------------------------------------- WAVEFORM BY NAME, not by number: :Sine :Triangle :Square :Saw.

methods.name: AddSound
methods.description: Play an existing sound (a stzSound, or an engine buffer id) as a source.

methods.name: AddTimeline
methods.description: MU2: a node whose output is the notes placed on it, each at the frame asked -- inside a block, not at its top. It has no input. Returns the node (1-based), which StzEngineSoundGraphTimelinePlace takes.

methods.name: AddGainOn
methods.description: the shapers: each takes WHAT it acts on, by name

methods.name: AddEnvelopeOnAt
methods.description: The same envelope, starting nStart seconds in. THIS is what makes a score possible: a voice that knows WHEN it sounds is a note.

methods.name: AddEchoOn
methods.description: ECHO, not "reverb". SN4's challenge pass refused to call a delay a reverb: one repeat fading out is not a diffuse room, and a name that promises a hall and delivers a slapback survives into documentation.

methods.name: AddMixOf
methods.description: mixing -------------------------------------------------------------- Mix several named nodes into one. The engine requires every input to EXIST before the mix does -- that is what makes a cycle impossible -- so this verb takes them all at once rather than letting you add to a mix later and discover the refusal.

methods.name: SetOutputTo
methods.description: output -------------------------------------------------------------- Which node the graph hands to the world. Defaults to the last thing added, which is right far more often than not.

methods.name: ToSound
methods.description: Render nSeconds and hand back a stzSound. DATA, so To... is right.

methods.name: Rewind
methods.description: Rewind every stateful node so the next render starts from the top.

methods.name: PlayFor
methods.description: hearing it

methods.name: Underruns
methods.description: How many frames the last PlayFor could not supply. Zero is the answer you want, and the plane counts it rather than letting you guess.

methods.name: Rows
methods.description: shape and meaning

methods.name: SecondsPerRow
methods.description: What one row STEP means in time, for a spectrogram. 0 when a row is not a moment (a spectrum, an onset list).

methods.name: HertzPerColumn
methods.description: What one column means in frequency. 0 when a column is not a frequency.

methods.name: PeakColumnOfRow
methods.description: Which column holds the largest value in a row -- "which frequency won".

methods.name: PeakFrequencyOfRow
methods.description: The same answer in hertz, which is what you actually wanted.

methods.name: ToList
methods.description: One row as a plain Haro list. DATA, so To... is right. It crosses the FFI once per value, so it is for looking at a row, not at a whole spectrogram -- ToCanvas does that without ever building a Haro list.

methods.name: ToTimesList
methods.description: The whole of a one-row grid -- an onset list is exactly this.

methods.name: ToCanvas
methods.description: Recorded as an SN5 finding: an AddImage on stzCanvas would turn this from thousands of rectangles into one call, and the graphics plane is where that belongs.

methods.name: ToCanvasOf
methods.description: pnMaxBins caps how much of the spectrum is drawn: nearly all musical energy lives in the bottom fraction of the range, and drawing 2048 bins up to Nyquist wastes most of the picture on silence.

methods.name: ToSVGFile
methods.description: Write the picture. SVG always works -- it needs no device at all, which is what lets a CI machine draw a spectrogram.

methods.name: ToPNG
methods.description: PNG goes through the GPU tier, so it needs a device. SVG does not.

methods.name: IsUsable
methods.description: what it is

methods.name: HonestName
methods.description: The name it ships under if the author's ear says the real one lies.

methods.name: PitchClass
methods.description: harmonic: held to 2 cents. inharmonic: a bar, a bell or a drum, whose partials are not multiples -- its lowest mode is checked, its perceived pitch is the listener's. none: a hi-hat or a snare.

methods.name: ToSoundOf
methods.description: a note, as data

methods.name: ToSoundOfGlide
methods.description: A pitch that MOVES while it sounds -- a talking drum squeezed, a bow sliding. Strings plucked and FM voices hold one pitch and refuse this.

methods.name: ToSoundOfStroke
methods.description: Where a drum is struck. Hand drums: :Dum (centre), :Tak (rim), :Ka (the weaker rim). The kit: :Kick, :Snare, :HiHat.

methods.name: RawCents
methods.description: what the last note needed

methods.name: SetTempo
methods.description: settings

methods.name: CaptureInsteadOfDevice
methods.description: WHAT IT CANNOT STAND IN FOR: a device drains on ITS OWN thread, so while this thread is busy rendering a new loop's notes the card keeps playing what was posted. Here THIS thread is the consumer, so it stalls with the render and nothing is consumed. Whether a render while playing costs a note its frame is therefore a DEVICE question, and the guard asks it on the device.

methods.name: LiveLoop
methods.description: NAMED LiveLoop, NOT Loop. The plan's section 4 writes oM.Loop(...), and that line cannot be written in Haro: `loop` is a keyword (it is Haro's `continue`), and a method may not take its name. LiveLoop is also Sonic Pi's word for the same thing (live_loop).

methods.name: LiveLoopOf
methods.description: A loop given a pattern object -- one already transformed by the algebra.

methods.name: Every
methods.description: The plan's line: every n cycles, the loop transformed. A redefinition like any other -- it lands on a boundary.

methods.name: Silence
methods.description: Stop one loop at the next boundary it can land on.

methods.name: Start
methods.description: running

methods.name: Tick
methods.description: Post what is due, drain (capture mode), and report what is heard.

methods.name: WaitCycles
methods.description: Play for `pnCycles` more cycles of HEARD time, ticking all the while.

methods.name: DriveWith
methods.description: The reactive plane drives it instead: one timer, every 20 ms, for every session registered -- see StzSoundLiveTickAll above for why it is global.

methods.name: Release
methods.description: Free the notes and the graph -- only once stopped: the timeline reads the notes' samples directly.

methods.name: IsRunning
methods.description: what happened

methods.name: HeardFrames
methods.description: Frames the listener has been given: the device's consumed frames, or what capture mode has drained.

methods.name: ConsoleLog
methods.description: [ cycle, heardFrame, text ] -- one line per cycle as it was HEARD

methods.name: Landings
methods.description: [ name, version, landingCycle, heardCycleAtCall ]

methods.name: MidCycleChanges
methods.description: Withdrawals the engine refused because the note was already sounding -- a change that would have landed MID-CYCLE. MU3's kill criterion is that this stays 0.

methods.name: ToABC
methods.description: ABC 2.1

methods.name: ToMusicXML
methods.description: MusicXML (partwise)

methods.name: ToMidiFile
methods.description: MIDI (Standard MIDI File, type 1)

methods.name: DistinctNotes
methods.description: The distinct notes and strokes over the first `pnCycles` cycles -- what a player renders BEFORE it starts: DistinctValues, in sound's word.

methods.name: IsAllStrokes
methods.description: True when every word is a stroke: the pattern names its own drum.

methods.name: ToScoreQ
methods.description: `pnCycles` cycles as a stzSoundScore, a cycle being four beats. The pivot: a pattern is a function, a score is data, and this is where one becomes the other.

methods.name: SetNote
methods.description: One line under the plot saying what the picture MEANS. A chart that needs a paragraph of explanation elsewhere is a chart that failed.

methods.name: ToNoteLines
methods.description: The note as it will actually be laid out -- DATA, so To... is right. It exists so a guard can check the wrapping without reading the picture: text reaches the SVG as glyph OUTLINES, not as characters, so there is nothing in the output to read the sentence back out of.

methods.name: DrawSpectrogram
methods.description: THE SPECTROGRAM ----------------------------------------------------- Time across, frequency up, magnitude as lightness. nMaxHz crops the top: nearly all musical energy lives low, and drawing to Nyquist spends most of the picture on silence.

methods.name: DrawSpectra
methods.description: THE SPECTRUM (one or more series) ----------------------------------- paSeries: [ [cLabel, oGrid], ... ] -- each a one-row spectrum grid. Log frequency across, decibels up. Several series is a CATEGORICAL job: fixed hue order, a legend always, and a direct label on each line.

methods.name: DrawWave
methods.description: THE WAVEFORM

methods.name: MarkTimeAt
methods.description: A vertical marker with a label -- for pointing at the moment something happens ("the click is HERE").

methods.name: MarkFrequencyAt
methods.description: The same marker on a LOG frequency axis -- for pointing at a filter's corner, a fundamental, or Nyquist. The from/to must match the DrawSpectra call, because the axis is only as wide as what was drawn on it.

methods.name: Spoken
methods.description: The syllable as SAPI says it, slowly -- the raw material, unretuned.

methods.name: Syllable
methods.description: The syllable held on a note (a name or Hz) for `pnSeconds`, at 48 kHz.

methods.name: LineQ
methods.description: Syllables on notes, a beat each, laid end to end.

methods.name: Sing
methods.description: SINGING -- gated by the retuned voice's own verdict.

methods.name: SetLookahead
methods.description: settings ------------------------------------------------------------ Frames of lookahead. Set it small only to PROVE the engine counts lateness -- the negative sibling in the guard does exactly that.

methods.name: Prepare
methods.description: the instruments' work, done first

methods.name: Play
methods.description: live, on the device

methods.name: Tick
methods.description: Post what is due, let the transport keep its clock, and stop once the last note has played out on the device.

methods.name: RenderThroughRing
methods.description: The SAME real-time path -- a producer thread rendering the graph into a ring, this thread posting notes ahead of it -- with this thread also draining the ring instead of a sound card. It runs as fast as the machine can, which is HARDER for the scheduler than a device: the producer is never waiting for the speaker. What comes out is returned as a sound, so a guard can hold it against the offline render sample for sample.

methods.name: Placed
methods.description: what happened

methods.name: Late
methods.description: Notes whose frame the producer had already rendered when they arrived.

methods.name: Underruns
methods.description: Frames the device asked for and the ring could not supply, as of the last tick -- the producer falling behind, which is a different failure from a note posted late, and counted separately.

methods.name: Release
methods.description: Free the notes. Only once nothing is playing: the timeline reads their samples directly, and a freed note under a playing timeline is a read of freed memory.

methods.name: Note
methods.description: building ------------------------------------------------------------ One pitched note, after everything already in the score. `pNote` is a note name ("A4", "C#3", "Bb2", "D4+50") or a frequency in Hz.

methods.name: GlideAt
methods.description: MU4: a note whose pitch MOVES from one pitch to another over its whole length -- a meend, a Zarma slide, a kalangu's squeezed tone. Names or Hz.

methods.name: NoteAt
methods.description: MU3: a note at an explicit beat, for a score built from a pattern. It does not move where the next Note() goes; the length grows to cover it.

methods.name: SetLength
methods.description: The length in beats, set outright -- a pattern's cycles end where they end, whatever their last note does.

methods.name: Stroke
methods.description: A struck sound on a membrane -- :dum, :tak, :ka, or :kick, :snare, :hihat on the kit. Which drum strikes it is the instrument's business (On).

methods.name: AddNotes
methods.description: Space-separated names, one beat each; the octave carries; ~ rests.

methods.name: Then
methods.description: the algebra --------------------------------------------------------- SEQUENCE: the other score starts where this one ends.

methods.name: Together
methods.description: PARALLEL: the other score starts where this one starts. The length is the longer of the two.

methods.name: Repeat
methods.description: The same score, n times in sequence.

methods.name: On
methods.description: AND it names the notes this score gains AFTERWARDS by Note and Stroke. The first cut was the pure modifier only, and the very first smoke test fell into it: StzSoundScoreQ().On(:Drumkit) then twenty strokes named NOTHING (the score was empty when On ran), so every stroke went to the default piano and was refused. A rule that the first user breaks in the first line is the rule's fault. Scores joined by Then or Together keep their own naming -- an unnamed part stays unnamed until an outer On names it.

methods.name: Transpose
methods.description: Semitones, fractional allowed (0.5 is a quarter tone). Strokes keep their pitch: a transposed drum pattern is the same drum pattern.

methods.name: SetVelocity
methods.description: The velocity of notes ADDED FROM NOW ON, 0 < v <= 1.

methods.name: Tempo
methods.description: the performance settings

methods.name: Quantize
methods.description: Snap every start to the nearest multiple of `pnGrid` beats (0.25 = a sixteenth). 0 turns it off. Durations are left alone.

methods.name: Swing
methods.description: SWING: the first of each PAIR of subdivisions lasts `pnRatio` of the pair. 0.5 is straight, 2/3 is a triplet swing, 0.75 a dotted one. Every position is warped, not only those on the grid -- the first half of each pair is stretched and the second compressed, piecewise-linearly -- so a note between two grid points moves with its neighbours instead of jumping past one.

methods.name: Events
methods.description: reading it ---------------------------------------------------------- The events in start order. A copy: changing it changes nothing here.

methods.name: PitchedEvents
methods.description: The plan's fourth transform: key, mode, density, contour -- Music21's side, on the same stzSoundScore every other transform makes and reads. the pitched events, in start order

methods.name: RangeInCents
methods.description: lowest to highest pitch, in cents

methods.name: Density
methods.description: pitched notes per beat

methods.name: Contour
methods.description: "U", "D" or "S" from each pitched note to the next -- S within 5 cents

methods.name: BestModes
methods.description: WHICH DECLARED MODE FITS: every mode of every universe, every note tried as its tonic, scored by how far (in cents) each note sits from the nearest degree of the mode, going up or coming down -- the mean. [ universe, mode, tonicHz, meanCentsOff ], best first. It ranks the DECLARATIONS; a tie is reported as a tie.

methods.name: FrameOf
methods.description: WHERE A BEAT LANDS, in 0-based frames at `pnRate`: quantised, then swung, then timed. The one place beats become frames -- the offline render and the live scheduler both call it, so they cannot disagree about when a note is.

methods.name: ToSound
methods.description: performing it ------------------------------------------------------- The whole performance, rendered offline into one sound. Every note is the instrument's (MU1), placed at FrameOf() by mixInto.

methods.name: Plan
methods.description: [ frame0, bufferId ] per event, in start order; rendered on first ask.

methods.name: BufferFor
methods.description: MU3: one note's buffer, rendered once -- the live loops ask for notes one at a time. [ start, beats, hz, instrument, velocity, stroke ]

methods.name: init
methods.description: present on purpose: "new X()" WITH parentheses calls init, and fails when there is none ("Calling Function without definition: init")

methods.name: State
methods.description: what it is doing

methods.name: Refusals
methods.description: How many moves the state machine refused. A transport that is being driven wrongly says so in a number rather than misbehaving quietly.

methods.name: PositionInFrames
methods.description: Frames the DEVICE has consumed, not frames the graph has produced: the producer runs ahead by a ring's worth, so asking it would report a position up to a third of a second in the future. What the listener has heard is what the device has taken.

methods.name: Underruns
methods.description: Frames the producer could not supply in time. Zero is the answer you want, and it is counted rather than guessed.

methods.name: Play
methods.description: the moves

methods.name: PlayFor
methods.description: Play, and stop by itself after pnSeconds. The stop happens in Tick(), so it needs someone to be ticking -- RunFor and DriveWith both do.

methods.name: Resume
methods.description: The graph carries on from where it was: pausing did not rewind it, so an envelope half way through its decay is still half way through it.

methods.name: Rewind
methods.description: Back to the top: the graph rewinds and the clock goes with it. Only legal when stopped, because rewinding under a running device is a jump.

methods.name: Tick
methods.description: being driven -------------------------------------------------------- One step. Cheap on purpose: it reads a counter and decides whether the sound has run out. Call it as often as you like.

methods.name: RunToEnd
methods.description: Tick until it stops, without a reactive loop. This DOES occupy the thread -- it is the honest version of PlayFor for a script that has nothing else to do, and it still reports the position while it runs.

methods.name: RunFor
methods.description: Same as PlayFor: Play, and stop by itself after pnSeconds. The stop happens in Tick(), so it needs someone to be ticking -- RunFor and DriveWith both do.

methods.name: DriveWith
methods.description: THE REACTIVE CONVERGENCE. The transport does not own a loop; it owns a STEP. Hand it a stzReactive and the loop that already exists calls the step, alongside every timer, stream and task that loop is already carrying -- which is the whole point of there being one loop.

methods.name: OnStarted
methods.description: what to call

methods.name: Release
methods.description: housekeeping

methods.name: Mode
methods.description: choosing

methods.name: NoCycle
methods.description: The phrase ALONE: a cycle of `pnBeats` with no layers and no accents -- to hear a mode without its rhythm, or to measure a melody note with nothing struck on top of it.

methods.name: CentsOf
methods.description: the pitch vocabulary ------------------------------------------------- Cents above the tonic of degree `pcDegree` ("5", "5_", "9"), reached going UP (pbDown FALSE) or DOWN. -1 when the mode declares no scale.

methods.name: Check
methods.description: The movement rules this mode declares, held against a phrase: a list of what breaks them, each as text. An empty list is a phrase the declaration permits -- not a phrase a musician would call right.

methods.name: PerformQ
methods.description: performing a phrase --------------------------------------------------- The phrase, once per cycle for `pnCycles` cycles, in this mode, over this cycle, with its ornaments and accents, as a stzSoundScore. One phrase cycle fills one rhythmic cycle, however many beats that has.

methods.name: Sentences
methods.description: The declared sentences of a TONAL language, drummed: the plan's MU7 row (text -> drum) needs the declaration first, and it is here. Each syllable is a stroke at the pitch its tone asks for -- High, Low, or a Falling glide from High to Low -- lasting its declared units (a long vowel takes two). The interval between High and Low is the declaration's :tonepitch, which says where it came from.

methods.name: SonifyQ
methods.description: The plan's MU7 row "data -> melody in a declared universe": sonification that a listener from the tradition would hear as music, not as a meter. The lowest value sits on degree 1 and the highest two octaves of the mode up; one note per beat of the cycle, the cycle's own rhythm under it, the mode's movement and ornaments applied as for any phrase. A series with no spread is refused rather than played as one repeated note.

methods.name: SonifiedDegrees
methods.description: the degrees the last SonifyQ chose, one per value

methods.name: SonifiedTop
methods.description: the highest degree it allowed -- 2n, or fewer when the instrument is short

methods.name: ToneSyllables
methods.description: ToneSyllables returns what was read; DrumTonesQ plays it on the drum. SayOnDrum is the verb the plan names, and it is GATED: text -> drum is speech only if a Hausa speaker hears the sentence back, and until one has (the declaration's :talkingdrum verdict), it refuses with that reason.

methods.name: PlayedNotes
methods.description: [ beat, degree, cents, hz, ornament ] for every melody note the last PerformQ placed -- what a guard, or a curious reader, holds it against.

methods.name: ExpectFindings
methods.description: A FRAME MAY BE ABOUT A PICTURE THE GATE FINDS FAULT WITH, and that is not a defect in the telling -- it is often the point. "Here is what goes wrong" is a frame whose picture is meant to be unlawful. So a frame says so, and then the gate's findings are its SUBJECT rather than its failure. A frame that expects findings and gets none is itself reported, because a flag nobody checks is a flag that rots.

methods.name: Bind

methods.name: BindFact
methods.description: A FACT FROM ANOTHER PLANE. The fact shape is one shape on purpose (DN9b), so a verdict an org chart reached, or a count a notation picture keeps, can be quoted in a caption about a drawing of it. The caller supplies the fact; the storyboard still holds the caption to it, which is the whole point of binding rather than typing.

methods.name: Show
methods.description: what a frame may do to the picture

methods.name: Act
methods.description: AN ACTION IS WHAT TURNS A PICTURE INTO A DEMONSTRATION. Between two frames something changes -- a point is dragged, a datum is set -- and the next frame shows what that did. The verbs are the picture's own.

methods.name: NumberOfFrames
methods.description: what the storyboard is, once written

methods.name: NumberOfHoles
methods.description: how many numbers this narration shows, all of them from facts

methods.name: Judge
methods.description: EVERY FRAME THROUGH THE GATE, EVERY HOLE HELD TO ITS FACT. The second half is what makes a filled caption evidence rather than decoration: the number the reader sees must be the number the fact reported, and a hole the author never bound must not survive into the sentence.

methods.name: Render
methods.description: the folio, and the page --------------------------------------------- The frames are already drawn, one file each, as they closed. This writes the page that puts them in order with their sentences.

methods.name: ToNarration
methods.description: The question of whether this shape conforms was routed to the sibling through Central as DN9-EMITTER-01 and is unanswered; silence is not a veto here, so this is written, pinned and marked, and a correction costs one function.

methods.name: Rendition
methods.description: A VALUE THAT SAYS WHAT IT IS (DN9g) --------------------------------- A STORYBOARD IS NOT A PICTURE, and its rendition says so by its kind: markup, the page that puts its frames in order. A consumer choosing a surface from the kind alone therefore opens it as a document rather than trying to draw it, without knowing what class it came from.

methods.description: The string with the HTML-special chars encoded as entities. Engine-backed. This built a per-character LIST of the whole string and concatenated onto a growing result -- the wrap-to-scan shape, quadratic in the string length. methods.name: ReduceWithPCA

methods.description: the inner analysis, when there was one -- so a caller can ask how much variance survived the reduction before reading anything into the picture

methods.name: LearnMapping
methods.description: IT IS A TRADE, not an upgrade. The embedding is generally somewhat worse than ordinary t-SNE, because free coordinates can go anywhere and a network's outputs are limited to what it can express.

methods.name: SetHiddenLayers
methods.description: The hidden layer widths. The output layer is always LINEAR and as wide as the embedding, because a coordinate is unbounded and squashing it through a tanh would cap the layout at a box.

methods.name: Transform
methods.description: Only available after LearnMapping(). Ordinary t-SNE has no map to apply, and manufacturing one by re-running the optimisation would be a different answer wearing the same name.

methods.name: PreserveDensity
methods.description: t-SNE reports its own objective, so unlike UMAP the price is directly visible: KL rises from 0.291 to 0.443 at the default. That is neighbourhood fidelity being spent on density fidelity, in the units of the thing given up.

methods.name: SetDensityWeight
methods.description: 0 turns the term off EXACTLY -- bit-for-bit the ordinary fit, not a near one. Values between about 1.5 and 3 are the unstable band described above.

methods.name: SetDensityPhase
methods.description: the FINAL fraction of iterations during which the term runs. Late on purpose, and for a reason t-SNE has that UMAP does not: EARLY EXAGGERATION multiplies P by 12 for the first quarter of the run to force gaps open, so density measured during it would preserve a scale the algorithm is about to throw away.

methods.name: DensityCorrelation
methods.description: how far the term got. NOT a percentage -- an embedding with every density rank backwards still scores around -0.6 rather than -1.

methods.name: LocalRadii
methods.description: Weighted here by t-SNE's joint distribution where stzUMAP weights by the fuzzy graph. Two different weightings of the same neighbourhoods, agreeing on which rows are dense.

methods.name: NewLocalRadii
methods.description: Available whether or not the fit preserved density, because it is a property of the data rather than of the map. the radii of the rows the last Transform() placed. The classic extension measures them on its way past; the parametric one cannot, so there it stays empty and LocalRadiiOf() is the way to ask.

methods.name: LearnInverse
methods.description: Two dimensions cannot hold six. The inverse recovers what the embedding KEPT and invents the rest: a plausible row for a location, never a recovered one.

methods.name: SetInverseEpochs
methods.description: a decoder is a REGRESSION problem and wants far more epochs than the embedding itself did -- measured, [32,32] at 3000 was three times WORSE than a plain lookup and [64,64] at 40000 a third better

methods.name: Inverse
methods.description: TAKE POINTS IN THE MAP, RETURN ROWS IN THE DATA. The points need not be positions of training rows -- somewhere between two clusters is exactly the question worth asking, and the answer is a plausible row for that location.

methods.name: Trustworthiness

methods.name: Chunks
methods.description: POS-PATTERN CHUNKING (R3, the NLTK offensive): PATTERNS OVER TAGS. ? Q("The quick brown fox...").TextQ().Chunks("DT? JJ* NN+") #--> [ "The quick brown fox", "the lazy dog" ] Grammar: Penn tags separated by spaces, each with an optional quantifier -- ? (0/1), * (0+), + (1+), none (exactly 1). A tag matches by PREFIX (NN covers NN/NNS/NNP/NNPS). Covers NLTK's RegexpParser chunking with a cleaner grammar. The executor is a deterministic greedy scanner over the tag stream (like NLTK's); a Listex-native executor can swap in behind this same surface.

methods.name: ReleaseGraph
methods.description: Give the engine's graph back. The next Fit() builds it again.

methods.name: SetNeighbors
methods.description: THE LOCAL/GLOBAL DIAL. Small values see fine structure and fragment; large values see the broad shape and smear detail. The reference implementation defaults to 15.

methods.name: SetMinDistance
methods.description: How tightly points may pack. Smaller packs tighter, which makes clusters look more separated -- an appearance you are choosing, not a finding.

methods.name: LearnFromLabels
methods.description: A supervised embedding WILL separate your classes. That is what you asked for. It is therefore NOT evidence that the classes are separable, and the picture must never be shown as if it were -- the separation is an input, not a finding. What it is genuinely good for: seeing structure WITHIN classes you already trust, and laying out data whose grouping is not in question so that something else can be looked at.

methods.name: SetTargetWeight
methods.description: MEASURED, and it is not the shape one would assume: separation rises to about 0.2 and then FALLS, and beyond ~0.9 the setting stops meaning anything at all because the penalty underflows. Crushing every cross-class edge fragments the graph -- points lose most of their neighbours and the classes come apart into pieces instead of two groups. More supervision is not more separation.

methods.name: PreserveDensity
methods.description: Getting the density right COSTS the separation between groups -- the term buys room by spending what the layout was using to hold clusters apart. There is no setting that is simply better: a high lambda answers "how dense is each region" at the expense of "how many groups are there", and the second is usually why the plot was opened. (Note this dial IS monotone, unlike SetTargetWeight() -- do not carry either shape over to the other.)

methods.name: SetDensityWeight
methods.description: how hard to push. 0 turns the term off entirely, and does so EXACTLY -- the run is bit-for-bit the ordinary fit rather than a near one.

methods.name: SetDensityPhase
methods.description: the FINAL fraction of epochs during which the term is active. It is switched on late deliberately: on a random start the embedded radii are noise, so their correlation with anything is noise, and its gradient is noise with a lever arm.

methods.name: DensityCorrelation
methods.description: It is NOT a percentage. An embedding that gets every density rank BACKWARDS can still score around -0.6 rather than -1, because reversing an order is not the same as negating it.

methods.name: LocalRadii
methods.description: This is a DATA PRODUCT, not a by-product of drawing: it ranks rows by isolation and is meaningful with no reference to the embedding at all. Use it to find outliers or to weight a downstream model. It costs nothing extra, because the density term has to compute it anyway.

methods.name: LearnMapping
methods.description: So if the point of supervising is to pull apart classes the geometry does NOT already separate, use SkipMapping() and take the free-form fit -- and give up the exact transform. That is the trade, stated rather than discovered later.

methods.name: SetLearningRate
methods.description: MEASURED, and the reason the gradient is AVERAGED per point rather than summed: with a summed epoch gradient a point's step was proportional to how many edges touched it, and at a learning rate only twice the default every point of a cluster collapsed onto the same output -- while the separation ratio reported 6471293, which reads like a triumph. Averaging made the whole range 0.005 to 0.05 behave. A summary ratio is never evidence on its own.

methods.name: LearnInverse
methods.description: Two dimensions cannot hold thirty. The inverse recovers what the embedding KEPT and invents the rest. It is a plausible row for a location, never a recovered one.

methods.name: SetInverseEpochs
methods.description: Hence the defaults of [64,64] and 15000. A decoder is a regression problem and wants far more epochs than the embedding itself did.

methods.name: Inverse
methods.description: The points do not have to be positions of training rows -- somewhere between two clusters is exactly the question worth asking, and the answer is a plausible row for that location rather than a recovered one.

methods.name: Trustworthiness
methods.description: THE WITNESS -- see stzTSNE.Trustworthiness(); the same engine call on the data the fit saw (the PCA scores when reducing) and the embedding

methods.name: CurveParameters
methods.description: The fitted similarity curve 1/(1 + a*d^(2b)). Reported because a and b are DERIVED from min_dist and spread by a least-squares fit rather than given, and a caller may reasonably want to see what their setting turned into.

methods.name: Transform
methods.description: This is not a refit. See the note at the top of this file for what that costs.

methods.name: NewLocalRadii
methods.description: Computed whether or not density preservation is on, because it is a property of the data rather than of the placement, and it costs nothing -- the transform has to measure those distances anyway.

methods.name: LocalRadiiOf
methods.description: It has to be the data rather than the map, and the parametric variant is why: a network saturates, so a row far outside the training range comes back 0.000001 from a legitimate one. The training set has not saturated -- 356 units from anything is 356 units from anything.

methods.description: Same as Search: The distance is SQUARED Euclidean over the stored vectors -- squared because the square root changes nothing about the ordering and costs a call per candidate. methods.name: RecallAgainstExact

methods.name: CosineFromDistance
methods.description: Cosine similarity of a stored vector to a query, recovered from the stored distance. Only meaningful in :Cosine mode, where both are unit vectors and d^2 = 2 - 2*cos.

An exact tag match is tried first, then a language-only match ("fr" finds "fr-FR") -- which is a WIDENING within one language, not a substitution across two. Anything else is a counted refusal, and the reason names what the machine actually has.

methods.name: SetRate
methods.description: SAPI takes rate -10..10 and volume 0..100 and IGNORES anything else. The engine clamps and reports, because a setting that silently does nothing is worse than one that is visibly limited.

methods.description: WARMING UP ---------------------------------------------------------- Pay the cold cost NOW, not in the middle of the first sentence. VC0 measured a cold synthesis at 4.3x a warm one -- the same trap SN0 found in ma_device_start, where start-up took 500 ms and callbacks ran ahead of real time during it. One inaudible syllable, discarded.

methods.name: SampleRate

methods.name: SynthesisIsTheBottleneck

methods.name: Poll
methods.description: the frame ----------------------------------------------------------- Pump the OS event queue and SAMPLE input. Everything the frame then reads -- keys, mouse, size, delta -- describes the same instant, so two reads in one frame cannot disagree with each other.

methods.name: DeltaTime
methods.description: Seconds since the previous Poll(). Multiply speeds by this and motion stops depending on how fast the machine happens to be -- the one number that separates an animation from a slideshow.

methods.name: FPS

methods.name: KeyDown

KeyPressed answers "did it go down since the last Poll" -- true exactly once per physical press, which is what a command wants. Written with only the first, pressing P once pauses and unpauses sixty times.
